title: docs(adr): ADR-0162 revised on two rulings of 2026-11-27: a closing outcome is written when the approval is over, and the document is held for the whole approval
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuVFphxD3X9wcs8Uwr3wfJaq)_

Fixes #37817

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Tier: H

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：用户无感，这次只改设计文档，把 11 月 27 日的两条裁定按原话写了进去：凡是声明了关闭状态的对象，每一次审批从提交到结束别人都改不了单据（退回修改期间、以及作者特意不上锁的步骤在等人审批时照旧可以改），而在审批结果会关闭单据的状态字段上，每一步的结果都等审批全部走完才显示，中途一直是「审批中」。
- 为什么做：属于「关闭状态锁」专题，后面的施工和测试要按新裁定做，所以设计文档先改；第一稿把「全程锁」写窄了，复核指出后已按裁定原话放宽。
- 出错会怎样：文档写错会让后面的施工按错的约定做，最坏是使用者看到单据在审批没走完时就显示「已批准」，或者单据在审批途中被人改动而审批人没看到；按原话放宽也有代价，声明了关闭状态的对象上连同关闭无关的审批在两步之间也不能再改单据，而且这类对象的审批要求服务器装有后台任务服务，否则审批开不了；这次只动文档，撤回这一次合并就恢复原文。
- 要你做什么：这是受管的架构记录修订，需要你审阅批准后才能合并。

## What changes

One file: `docs/adr/0162-an-object-declares-its-closed-states-the-record-and-its-lines-are-closed-to-change.md`, +220 / −61. No code, no generated file, no changeset. The record's row in `docs/adr/README.md` does not change, because the status line keeps its opening words.

The revision writes the maintainer's two rulings of 2026-11-27 into ADR-0162 (ruling record [`7210179412`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/37767#issuecomment-7210179412) on the design card), in place, with the seat's rulings on the design note where the record speaks to them. After the contract review of the first draft, the seat read both rulings by the words that were ruled (seat rulings [`7211509661`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/37817#issuecomment-7211509661) and [`7211531658`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/37817#issuecomment-7211531658) on the card), and this head carries that reading.

- **Status line and header.** The status keyword stays `Proposed`. The line gains "**Revised 2026-11-27** …" after the text it had. The header gains one bullet, "Ruled twice more on 2026-11-27", which quotes both rulings with the date, quotes the option the maintainer read for the second, names the four statements they replace, and names the seat's two rulings on how the words are read.
- **D5, first ruling: 「全部走完才显示已批准」.** A new block, "On a field the object closes on, a step's decision is written when the approval is over for the record". On a mirror field the object closes on at `approved` or `rejected`, every step's decision is held back, whichever of the two the object closes on, and the field keeps `pending`. The outcome is written when the approval is over for the record and has finished. Every other status is written as it is on `main`. A second paragraph, "How the plugin learns that an approval is over", gives the door's reading of the run, the mark on the request, the reconciler and the host it needs.
- **D5, second ruling: 「随新能力一起全程锁」.** A new block, "On an object that declares `closedStates`, a document under approval is held for the whole of the approval". The pending lock holds on through every passage, from each decision until the next request opens, the approval is over or it is abandoned. The hold covers every approval on such an object, whatever field it mirrors onto, and does not follow a node's `lockRecord`. It keeps three things of the pending lock: the revise window, a caller's delete of the record, and the passes for a system context and for a write of the mirror field alone. It ships with the key.
- **D5, the conditions.** Six become five. The condition that no user-run flow writes the record between two steps is withdrawn, in a paragraph of its own. The condition on a pause is kept and its reason restated. A host with no `job` service is a new ground of refusal at the first request, for every approval on an object that declares the key.
- **D5, what the conditions do not reach.** A refused write of the mirror is reported and not swallowed. An approval whose run ends between two steps is abandoned at once. A failure the flow routes to its end with the next step never asked counts as not finished.
- **D9.** The one lock read answers `approval` in a passage. The approvals-family read stays as published and does not answer for a passage.
- **Execution.** Item 7 records the carrying run and stamps the between-set on every approval on an object that declares the key, and its check no longer reads which nodes write the record. Item 8 is restated whole: the refused write, the outcome when the approval is over, the reconciler, the hold, the docs.
- **Consequences, Alternatives, Points the ruling does not settle, D10, TL;DR, Provenance, Readings, Refs** follow, so that no section still states the merged timing as the rule.

### Rework after the contract review

The contract review of the first draft ([`7211480053`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/37829#issuecomment-7211480053), on head `906da0f2`) found one must-fix, two should-fix and five nits. The seat then ruled how the two rulings are read. This head answers each finding:

| Finding | What the record says now |
|---|---|
| M1 (a): the hold did not reach an approval that closes on nothing | The hold covers every approval on an object that declares `closedStates`, in every passage (D5, "It covers every approval on an object that declares `closedStates`"). Every such approval carries the mark, is reconciled, and is refused on a host with no `job` service. The narrow reading is in Alternatives as not chosen, with what the wide one costs. |
| M1 (b): the passage after a decision that was not held back | On a field the object closes on at `approved` or `rejected`, every step's decision is held back, whichever value the object closes on (D5, "A decision the object does not close on is held back with the rest"). The three sentences the review found untrue of that case are true of it now. The by-value reading is in Alternatives, with why the record departs from the design note's sentence. |
| M1: the option the maintainer read | Quoted beside the ruling record's sentence, in the header bullet and at the head of the hold block. |
| S1: the hold followed `lockRecord`, on a reason that did not hold | The hold does not follow `lockRecord`. A node that declares `lockRecord: false` leaves the record open while its own request waits, as the key's published words say, and the passage after its decision is held. D5 and Alternatives give the corrected reason, and the sentence the review quoted is gone. |
| S2: the approvals-family read was widened while said to stay as published | It stays as published and does not answer for a passage. D9 quotes the contract's words. The header, items 2, 6 and 8 and ▲4 agree with it. What that costs a client is in Consequences. |
| N1: two summary sentences promised more than the rule | Both are rewritten and say where the hold lets go: the Consequences bullet under "What gets better", and D9's bullet on the two producers. |
| N2: who the revise window is open to | Every caller who may edit, as ADR-0044 D6 has it: in D5, in the "Returned" row, in Consequences, and in a new Readings row. |
| N3: two Alternatives argued from the merged timing | Both are reworded: "Judge each request as it opens" and "Let the mirror answer for an earlier step's field". |
| N4: indirect writes in a passage | D5 and Consequences say that an indirect write which carries no run of the approval is refused, that the node's failure abandons the approval, and that such a flow is abandoned on every submission. Item 8's hold part pins which indirect writes carry the run. See the note under this table. |
| N5: the mark of a record deleted in a passage | Item 8: the approval is marked abandoned, its marks are cleared, nothing is written, and the reconciler neither tries again nor notifies. |

**One point for the delta review, on N4.** The seat asked for the sentence that indirect writes in a passage are refused. The record says it of an indirect write that carries no run of the approval, and leaves to the build which indirect writes carry one. The reason is a reading of `main`, taken and not run. The lock reads a writer's run from the write's provenance (`packages/objectql/src/engine-execution-plumbing.ts#buildProvenance`), and the contexts a hook's api derives are spread from the context of the write that fired the hook (`packages/objectql/src/engine-scoped-context.ts#withRunAs`). So a hook's write-back inside a node's own write may carry that node's run, and pass the hold as it passes the pending lock today. An unqualified "refused" could be untrue of that case. The reading is one of the new Readings rows.

### Every statement the design note's section 5 names

All are revised. None is kept as it stood.

| The note names | What the revision does |
|---|---|
| D5: "The mirror writes each request's outcome as it is decided." | Revised. The mirror paragraph now says it writes each status as the request takes it, "with the one exception the ruling of 2026-11-27 makes": on a field the object closes on at `approved` or `rejected`, a step's decision is written when the approval is over. The rule is the new block that follows. |
| D5: "A record is on a closed value of its approval field in four situations only", whose second situation goes | Revised to three. The second situation, an approval passing from one step's decision to the next step's opening, is gone. The last now names the one case that is left: an approval that was not judged. |
| D5: "Two passes of the pending lock do not carry over", for a node after the last step | Revised. The nodes between two steps and after the last one read `pending` and meet no closed record. This lock refuses what comes after the outcome: a node that runs on after a pause that follows the last step, and any other flow or hook that acts as the caller. |
| D5: the reason given for condition 5 (no user-run flow writes the record between two steps) | The condition is withdrawn, in the paragraph "The condition that is withdrawn". With the outcome held back the record is not closed between two steps, and the hold passes the approval's own runs. The note proposes the same. |
| D5: the reason given for condition 6 (no pause between two steps) | Kept, reason restated: during such a pause the document would read `pending`, held, with no request open, and nobody would have a verb to end it. The note proposes the same. |
| D5: the premise of the first three bullets of "What the conditions do not reach" | Revised. None of the three now leaves a document closed on an unfinished approval. The bullets say what each leaves: a reported refusal and a held document that reads `pending`; an approval abandoned at once; a decision whose run cannot be resumed, which the reconciler ends. |
| D5: "Approved again … its request opens and the field holds `pending` once more" | Revised and split in two: "Approved, where another step follows" (nothing is written, the hold keeps the record) and "Approved at the approval's last step" (the field keeps `pending`, held, until the approval is over). |
| Consequences: the sentence that includes the steps after an approval decision among refused writers | Revised to its opposite: "That does not include the nodes that run straight after an approval decision (ruled 2026-11-27)". It then says what is still refused, an indirect write that carries no run of the approval among it, and what a flow that reacts to the field sees. |
| Consequences: the sentence that a record is open again while the next step is pending | Revised. The mirror writes `pending` as the approval's first request opens, and the document reads `pending` until the approval is over, "between two steps too, where nothing is written (ruled 2026-11-27)". The same bullet says where it is held meanwhile. |
| Consequences: two bullets under what it costs | Revised. The six-condition bullet now gives five. The bullet on a user-run write between two steps is replaced by the costs of the new rules: every approval on an object that declares the key needs a host with a `job` service; a fault between two steps costs a resubmission; a document reads `pending` for longer, also for a decision the object does not close on; the hold keeps callers out of every approval on such an object; a pause the conditions do not refuse holds the document; the request gains the mark and the plugin a reconciler. |
| Alternatives: "Hold a step's outcome back until the approval is over" | Moved to chosen, for a field the object closes on, with why the record first turned it down and what changed. |
| Alternatives: the narrow form of "Set the object's validation rules aside" | Decided against (ruled 2026-11-27), with the reasons the note gives. |
| Execution: item 7's "Between two steps is after one step's closed outcome" | Revised: after a step is decided, whichever way, and before the next step opens. |
| Execution: item 8 | Restated whole for the two rulings and the seat's rulings. |

### Statements revised beyond that list, so that the record agrees with itself

- The heading of the rule under the third ruling of 2026-11-26 loses two words: "would stop or hold it between two steps" becomes "would hold it". The condition that concerned a stop is the one withdrawn. The ruling's own words, 「平台拒绝这种配置」, stand. The seat kept this change.
- D5: the intro to the conditions; the reasons of the conditions on `readonlyWhen` and on the one mirror field; what "between two steps" means; the paragraphs "Otherwise the node refuses" and "What the conditions keep out"; the rows "While the request is pending", "Rejected", "Returned" and "Abandoned" of what a decided document shows; the abandoned rule, which now also covers an approval abandoned because its run ended between two steps.
- D5, one sentence under the second ruling of 2026-11-26. The record's own account of when an approval may have let a record be edited said "for as long as it ran, under a node that does not lock". It now says "while a request was pending under a node that does not lock", because the passages are held. The ruling's words and the option's text stand.
- D9: who produces a lock, what the approvals-family read answers in a passage, and one sentence on the record page's approvals part, which keeps its `lock` as the approvals-family read answers it. Two rows of the D10 table.
- "Points the ruling does not settle": the eighth of the fourteen points is marked withdrawn, and four new lists separate what the seat read from the rulings' words, the seat's rulings on the design note, the design note's own, and this record's own readings.
- TL;DR, Provenance, the Readings table (21 new rows, read at `ff9ee21084`) and Refs.
- Alternatives gains the narrower timing as considered and not taken, the options the two rulings turned down, and the readings the first draft took and the seat did not: a hold only where decisions are held back, a hold that follows `lockRecord`, a decision written at once where the object does not close on it, and an answer for a passage on the approvals-family read.

### Readings that are this record's own

Neither the rulings nor the seat's rulings speak to these. Each is listed as this record's own in "Points the ruling does not settle". They are for the delta review to confirm or send back.

1. **The five conditions are not widened.** A pause between two steps of an approval they do not concern is not refused, and the hold keeps the document through it. Consequences states the cost, and Alternatives has the other reading.
2. **An approval the node did not read when it opened is not held between its steps**: one that opened before the object declared the key, or whose requests the plugin could not place.
3. **Where the run of an approval that holds nothing back ends between two steps, the hold ends and the mirror writes nothing**, as on `main`.
4. **An indirect write in a passage that carries no run of the approval is refused**, and the build pins which indirect writes carry one (the note on N4 above).
5. **The approval of a record deleted in a passage is ended as abandoned**, with nothing written and its marks cleared.
6. **The condition on a write between two steps is withdrawn and the condition on a pause is kept.** The design note proposes both, and the card leaves the choice to the revision.
7. **The reasons of the conditions on `readonlyWhen` and on the one mirror field are restated** for the new timing. The conditions themselves stand.
8. **"Between two steps" is counted from every decision of a step**, since every decision is held back or begins a passage.
9. **Item 7's check no longer reads which nodes write the record**, since the condition that needed it is withdrawn.

## Why

ADR-0162 was merged on 2026-11-26 with the mirror writing each step's outcome as it is decided. The design of its Execution item 8 showed what that timing costs: a fault in the instant between two steps, or a rule of the app that refuses the put-back, leaves a document closed on an approval that did not finish. The maintainer ruled on 2026-11-27 to write the closing outcome only when the approval is over, and to hold the document for the whole approval, shipped with the key. The build cards cut from the record pin its statements in tests, so the record is revised first.

The first draft of the revision read the second ruling narrowly: a hold only where an outcome is held back, and only under a node that locks. The contract review found that narrower than the words that were ruled, and the seat ruled that the words stand. Widening the hold after the key is released would change shipped behaviour, which is what shipping the hold with the key avoids.

## Tests

None: the diff is one Markdown file under `docs/adr/`. Every code reading the revision adds was read at `ff9ee21084` and not run, and the record says so above the new Readings table. All 21 new rows are symbol anchors, file anchors or a link to ADR-0044, and `pnpm check:adr-symbol-anchors` resolves the anchors.

## Acceptance notes

Against the card's "Done when":

- **One PR revises ADR-0162, Tier H.** This one. `docs/adr/**` is governed, so it stays a draft and lands by the maintainer's hand.
- **Every statement the note's section 5 names is revised or kept with a reason.** The table above.
- **The status line stays `Proposed`.** It does, and the README row is byte-identical.
- **The two rulings are quoted with their dates.** In the header bullet, in D5 at the head of each of the two blocks, in the TL;DR and in "Points the ruling does not settle". The fuller sentences of the ruling record are quoted once each in D5, and the option the maintainer read for the second ruling is quoted beside it.
- **No sentence in the words of an earlier maintainer ruling changes.** Measured again on this head: the seven distinct 「…」 quotations in the record at the merge base all stand in the revised text, each as many times as before, and every blockquote is unchanged. The paragraphs that carry them changed only in this record's own sentences.

Not done here, on purpose:

- **No amended status keyword and no new ADR.** The record is `Proposed`, implements nothing, and the revision is in place, as the card orders.
- **`docs/adr/README.md` is not regenerated.** `pnpm adr:index` rewrites one row, ADR-0160's, whose status text changed on `main` without the index. That is outside this card. `pnpm check:adr-index` reports it as a warning and exits 0 by design.
- **The two things the design note found beside the card** are not decided here. The record cites one of them only as a reading of `main`, the stranded-request reader's bound of 500 rows read in no order, because the reconciler takes that reader's place for an approval on an object that declares the key.

## Verification

**Read first** (by risk):

1. D5, "On an object that declares `closedStates`, a document under approval is held for the whole of the approval": the second ruling as the seat read it. The bullets on its scope, on `lockRecord` and on what it keeps of the pending lock are where the first draft failed review.
2. D5, "On a field the object closes on, a step's decision is written when the approval is over for the record", with "How the plugin learns that an approval is over" under it: the first ruling as a rule, the decision held back by field and not by value, and the definitions of over, finished and ended between two steps that every later statement uses.
3. D9, "The approvals-family read stays exactly as published", with Execution item 8's hold part: a published read that does not answer for a passage, and what the hold card pins.
